comparison.brep_patches: Bidirectional evaluated surface witnesses, constrained to matching natural boundaries; same epsilon as fitted curves/surfaces.

scope_notes: Independent implementation based on public command/SDK outputs. No proprietary source inspected.
Fitting is sampled, not a continuous error certificate.
First radius uses Circle positive size getter. Second radius uses signed magnitude; zero/tiny second radius makes an unchanged point map.
Rigid always starts No. Copy getter edits persist on cancellation. First radius remembers when accepted and survives Undo/Redo/New.
Unchanged geometry still creates an Undo entry. Line results use a degree-one NURBS representation.
Repeated Copy uses originals and one history group. Undo retains empty cloned group definitions.
Radius diagnostics append Cancel. If Maelstrom already succeeded, that later command owns selection cleanup on Redo.
Native preference queries reaccept the exact integer radius they observed. Recipes intentionally restrict preference radii to integers so rounded prompt text cannot alter their value.

At this capture milestone, interactive workflows remained pending. Later input coverage is recorded in docs/maelstrom-input-provenance.json; Circle alternative modes and deformed previews remain pending.
Original native kernel performance comparison remains unverified.
Native box fitting changes UV correspondence tangentially. A public SDK/ClosestPoint diagnostic distinguishes parameter errors from physical geometric distances without enlarging epsilon.

A first radius point uses full distance and changes the Circle plane through the preferred-normal/parallel-Y fallback rule. A second radius point projects to that plane and rejects zero radial distance. Numeric second radii accept zero/tiny values as unchanged maps.
